first.rationale: Two of the three current signals are internal funnel decay (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), not purely competitive price pressure. Onboarding friction sits upstream of activation, so fixing it plausibly addresses both, and it buys revenue without structurally discounting it — the best fit for a 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective. I am spending verification on the two memories where a wrong inheritance would be most costly. memory_73 is the memory most likely to be acted on wrongly this week: it is the obvious reflex against a competitor's entry pricing, it carries unusually broad and elaborated claims (acquisition lift, revenue lift, faster time-to-first-value, holds across both billing plans) of the kind that tend to accumulate through consolidation rather than measurement, and its failure mode is invisible in-quarter — discount-acquired, price-shopping SMB cohorts can post strong short-run numbers while degrading retention, margin, and the quality of the revenue base. If the archive shows that record was short-horizon or measured only acquisition, promotional pricing should be off the table this week regardless of how well it matches the competitive story. memory_86 and memory_31 make overlapping claims about shortening/simplifying onboarding and may be the same underlying experiment consolidated twice; if so, my chosen direction rests on one study, not two, and the apparent weight of evidence behind it is inflated. Verifying memory_86 tests whether it is independent of memory_31 and whether its 'across self-serve accounts' scope is real or generalized. I am committing to a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout precisely because that duplication question is open, and I will hold a guardrail on activation quality (first meaningful action, not just completion) so that stripping onboarding steps does not simply push under-prepared accounts through the funnel — the same substitution-of-a-proxy-for-the-goal risk that discounting carries. If verification undercuts the onboarding record, activation_messaging (memory_91) is the fallback, since it targets the larger declining metric with a lighter footprint. enterprise_sales_assist is well-supported but addresses neither current decline this week.
